title: Seeking Help: Early Intervention Programmes and Medical Support
summary: If you have any concerns about your child’s development, the first step is to speak with the paediatrician—request a developmental screening, as it is your child’s right. In many countries, there are free or subsidised 'Early Intervention' programmes for children under three years old, and you do not need a final diagnosis to enrol. Also, reach out to the nursery or teachers, as they see your child in a different social context. Psychological support for parents is just as important—the worry about development is stressful, and seeking help is a strength, not a weakness.
try_this: This week: Book an appointment with the paediatrician to discuss any concerns (even if minor). Before the appointment: Write down three specific questions, bring short videos of your child in different situations, and request a referral to an early intervention programme if needed. Do not wait for the 'next appointment.'
reflection_prompts: What is your biggest fear about visiting the doctor to discuss your child’s development, and how can you ease it?
Who in your circle (family, friends, specialists) can be a support for you on this journey?
